studies.officialTitle: A Phase 1b/2a, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled, Study of the Safety, Tolerability, Pharmacokinetics, and Pharmacodynamics of Multiple Ascending Doses of GSBR-1290 in Adult Overweight or Obese Healthy Subjects and in Subjects With Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus on Metformin

design.description: Multi-cohort, multiple-ascending-dose study: Cohorts 1-3 (4-week, once-daily dose-ranging at 30/60/90 mg in overweight/obese participants), Cohort 4 (12-week, once-daily 120 mg in overweight/obese participants), and Cohort 5 (12-week, once-daily 45 mg or 90 mg in participants with type 2 diabetes on stable metformin).

studies.population: Adults who are overweight or obese (BMI 27-40 kg/m^2) without diabetes (Cohorts 1-4); adults who are overweight or obese (BMI 27-40 kg/m^2) with type 2 diabetes mellitus on stable metformin therapy for at least 6 months (Cohort 5).
studies.safetySummary: Adverse events were predominantly gastrointestinal (nausea, vomiting), most common at higher doses; 88-96% of adverse events were mild to moderate. Discontinuation due to adverse events was 0% in the overweight/obese cohorts and 2.8% (1/36) in the type 2 diabetes cohort. No serious adverse events were assessed as related to study drug, and no drug-induced liver injury was observed.

design.description: Part 1: open-label, 2-period, 2-sequence crossover comparing single-dose capsule and tablet formulations for bioavailability (Sequence 1: capsule Day 1, then tablet Day 8; Sequence 2: tablet Day 1, then capsule Day 8). Part 2: double-blind, placebo-controlled, 12-week once-daily tablet dosing across three cohorts, each cohort randomized to active drug or matched placebo (Cohort 3 additionally alternates between capsule and tablet formulation, active or placebo, for Weeks 9-12). Exact per-cohort doses were not disclosed in the sources reviewed; only an aggregate, dose-unattributed Part 2 efficacy figure was found (see case-scoped fallback in the research report).

studies.population: Healthy adults who are overweight or obese (BMI >=27 kg/m^2), 18-75 years.
studies.safetySummary: Across this study and the concurrent Phase 1b/2a obesity study, gastrointestinal adverse events (nausea, vomiting) were the most common treatment-emergent adverse events; discontinuation due to adverse events was reported in the range of 5% (obesity study) to 11% (this study), with no drug-induced liver injury observed. A per-cohort adverse-event breakdown was not disclosed.

studies.officialTitle: A Phase 2b, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled, Dose-range Finding Study of the Efficacy and Safety of Multiple Doses of Aleniglipron (GSBR-1290) in Participants Living With Obesity (Body Mass Index >= 30 kg/m2) or Overweight (Body Mass Index >= 27 kg/m2) With at Least One Weight-related Comorbidity

design.description: 36-week double-blind, placebo-controlled, dose-ranging trial of once-daily oral aleniglipron (5 mg starting dose, escalated every 4 weeks to a 45 mg, 90 mg, or 120 mg target dose), followed by an optional 36-week open-label extension (Weeks 36-72) in which all continuing participants (regardless of double-blind-period dose) were escalated further, every 4 weeks, toward a 180 mg target dose reached only after Week 60; the prior-placebo group crossed over at Week 36 starting at 2.5 mg onto the same 180 mg target-dose pathway. Exact intermediate titration steps for the open-label extension are not disclosed.

studies.population: Adults (18-79 years) with obesity (BMI >=30 kg/m^2) or overweight (BMI >=27 kg/m^2) with at least one obesity-related comorbidity, without diabetes.
studies.overallDuration: 36 weeks (double-blind period), plus an optional 36-week open-label extension
studies.safetySummary: Gastrointestinal adverse events, chiefly nausea and vomiting, were the most common treatment-emergent adverse events during the double-blind period, generally mild to moderate, decreasing in frequency over time with little recurrence of vomiting after dose interruption and retitration. Discontinuation due to adverse events was 5.4% with placebo and 13.3%, 7.7%, and 11.1% with the 45 mg, 90 mg, and 120 mg doses respectively. No drug-induced liver injury or QTc prolongation was observed; systolic blood pressure decreased in a dose-dependent manner (-7.9 to -9.0 mmHg with active treatment versus -1.5 mmHg with placebo). Anti-drug antibody incidence was not reported. During the open-label extension (through Week 72), overall discontinuation due to adverse events was reported only as an aggregate under 5% (not broken out by origin group); the prior-placebo crossover group had improved gastrointestinal tolerability versus the original 5 mg double-blind starting dose; no drug-induced liver injury was observed, and liver-enzyme elevations resolved without discontinuation. No per-group serious adverse event, nausea, vomiting, or anti-drug antibody figures were disclosed for the open-label extension.

studies.officialTitle: A Phase 2, Randomized, Double-blind, Placebo-controlled, Study Evaluating the Effects of Aleniglipron (GSBR-1290) on Body Composition in Participants Living With Obesity

design.description: Trial evaluating body-composition effects (total body fat mass by DXA, visceral adipose tissue, lean mass, body weight, waist circumference) of once-daily oral aleniglipron versus placebo (5:1 randomization). Per Structure Therapeutics' March 2026 disclosure, participants initiate aleniglipron at a 2.5 mg starting dose and titrate monthly to a 120 mg target dose. CORRECTION (2026-09-15): a prior pass mis-stated this trial's target dose as 180 mg, apparently cross-attributed from the separate ACCOMPLISH-1/ACCOMPLISH-2 Phase 3 dosing (45/90/180 mg); the September 2026 8-K exhibit cited for that figure does not mention any dose for this trial at all, and no source anywhere states a 180 mg dose for the Body Composition study specifically - reverted to the sole directly-supported figure, 120 mg. Per the registry, dosing spans approximately 40 weeks with primary/secondary DXA outcome measures assessed at Week 44; Structure's own August 2026 earnings-release language separately describes the trial as assessing body fat loss 'over a 44-week evaluation period,' updating the March release's '40-week evaluation period' phrasing - both are recorded with their own sourcing rather than merged into one unstated sentence.

studies.population: Adults (18-79 years) with obesity (BMI >=30 kg/m^2), without diabetes (HbA1c <6.5%) and without an endocrine cause of obesity (e.g. Cushing's syndrome, Prader-Willi syndrome, MC4R deficiency).
studies.overallDuration: Approximately 40 weeks of dosing (registry); primary/secondary DXA outcome measures at Week 44 (registry); described by the sponsor's most recent (August 2026) disclosure as a 44-week evaluation period, updating its own March 2026 '40-week evaluation period' phrasing
studies.safetySummary: An interim disclosure (71 participants enrolled) indicated that initiating treatment with a lower 2.5 mg starting dose improved tolerability, with no adverse-event-related discontinuations reported during the initial dosing period. Full efficacy and safety results were not yet available as of this research; topline data were expected in Q4 2026.
